files_reviewed: src/** (grep for env, localStorage, setTimeout, toast, console.log, TODO, innerHTML, useMutation)
note: Convex backend with all OpenAI, Firecrawl and AgentMail calls in server actions, so no ai_browser_call and no secret_exposure. No committed .env, .env.local or .env.keys. .env.example lists names only and VITE_ only carries the Convex URL. No database_rules labels: Convex has no RLS, and every client-facing function derives the renter server-side through requireOwned or getRenter. The AgentMail webhook verifies its Svix signature. No ai_tool_unbounded: sends, scrapes and audits are rate limited and capped at 8 emails per thread, and the model has no tool calling. UI toasts follow real awaited mutations, so no fake_action. Drafts pass a code policy check before sending, but several prompt rules have no matching check.

labels.what: With autopilot on, saveDraft queues each model-written email to a real landlord with no per-email approval. An inbound reply also schedules the next draft on its own (lines 815-816), so whole conversations run unattended. SignIn.tsx line 15 tells users they approve every email

When the model, or the regex fallback, reads an untrusted landlord email as a rejection, applyAnalysis sets the thread to declined, declines proposed tours and discards drafts with no renter review. The renter cannot reopen it, because approve, rewrite and chooseTour all refuse once the stage is declined. The comment at lines 654-657 calls this reversible bookkeeping

Rule to never invent competing offers, other applicants, deadlines, urgency or market statistics. policyViolations only checks commitment words and budget figures, so an invented offer or deadline passes and can go out on autopilot
Rule to state only facts listed under RENTER FACTS or LISTING FACTS. No code compares draft claims against the facts
Rule to never accept a rent, fee or term for the renter. The COMMITMENT regex catches sign, pay, wire, deposit and SSN wording but not acceptance phrases such as agreeing to a rent
Rule to ask for at most two concessions, only from ALLOWED ASKS. chooseAsks caps the input list, but nothing checks the draft output for extra or different asks
Rule to stay under 170 words with no emojis. finalizeDraft only appends a rationale note past 210 words and never blocks. Emojis are not checked
Second half of the budget rule: never say or imply the renter is comparing or touring other homes. Budget figures are checked in code, this part is not

Rule that clauseQuote must be copied word for word from the lease. The quote check runs only for the bundled sample (lines 137-141). Uploaded PDFs save model flags with no quote check (lines 197-203). leaseSchema.ts lines 105-109 says so

Demo landlord is a scripted counterparty: concessionFor (lines 92-152) always grants one concession and script() offers two made-up tour times, with a random 4-8 s fake thinking delay (mail.ts lines 338 and 523). Replies enter through the same ingest as real email. Labelled as demo in the UI

Sample lease check returns the pre-written CANNED_SAMPLE_AUDIT when OpenAI is missing or the sample quota is used. leaseAuditor.ts line 154 also falls back to it on any model error. The summary says no model wrote it
Scout discover loads bundled sample listings instead of searching the web when no Firecrawl key is set. It is labelled as demo mode in the feed
Six invented listings with fictional landlord names, 555 phone numbers and Unsplash photos, scaled to the renter's budget. Stored with isSample true and labelled in the UI
Fictional sample lease text and a hand-written review (CANNED_SAMPLE_AUDIT) with fixed flags
CLI seed renter Jordan Avery with a fixed, predictable passport token devseed000... If run on production, that Passport is public by a guessable token
CLI-only ensureDemoListing inserts a hardcoded Maple Court listing with a fixed match score of 88
Hardcoded demo landlord address on .example and six persona names used for simulated threads
Landing page story: fictional renter, landlord, listing, feed lines and a $50 rent win. Captions say it is an illustration
Landing dashboard fragment with hardcoded pipeline cards and stats (3 replies, 1 tour, $50/mo negotiated)
Landing ledger with a hardcoded before and after negotiation result. It is captioned as an illustration, not a promise

Password sign-up has no email verification. The only gate on emailing real landlords is isGuest false (threads.ts lines 273-277), so any throwaway account can make Nestor send AI email to any address the renter types in setContactEmail. Rate limits cap the volume
Demo landlord compose calls OpenAI with no rate limiter. Guests are one click to create and sample threads are free to start, so only BEATS=3 per thread bounds the spend, with no global ceiling
Paid reading of landlord replies is limited per thread only (inboundAnalysis keyed by thread id), with no deployment-wide ceiling like the other OpenAI paths
CLI test helper borrows any non-Nestor inbox in the AgentMail account when it cannot create one, and can reply from it. mail.ts lines 93-94 says no other inbox is ever touched
Renter instructions are joined into the prompt as private instructions without quarantine tags. Only the post-draft policyViolations check guards the output
UI says autopilot stops after 10 emails to real landlords a day, but limits.ts sets sendExternalEmail to 6 a day per renter and 15 a day globally
The 170-word limit is typed into the prompt text and into the EmailDraft schema description (aiSchemas.ts line 30) instead of reading MAX_BODY_WORDS (line 16)
A second set of lease-check caps (3 a day per renter, 25 a day global for the sample) lives here, apart from limits.ts (5 and 10 for uploads). All quotas are code constants
Model IDs and fallbacks hardcoded in code
Demo capture script hardcodes the production convex.site URL and a localhost dev URL. Lines 93-96 also hardcode a rehearsal password for throwaway dev accounts
